html:
An affirmative action programme in Malaysia, begun in 1971, that favoured ethnic Malays and other indigenous groups in business, education and jobs. It shaped the country for decades.

It was a response to the 13 May incident of 1969, when race riots broke out in Kuala Lumpur and hundreds died. Malays were the majority and held political power, but most were poor farmers, while Chinese Malaysians dominated trade and the cities. The government of Abdul Razak decided that peace needed a fairer share of wealth.

The policy had two stated goals: to end poverty for all races, and to end the link between race and economic role. It set a target for Bumiputera, the Malays and other indigenous peoples, to own 30 percent of company shares by 1990. Tools included university quotas, contracts and state companies.

Poverty fell sharply and a Malay middle class grew. Critics say the benefits went mostly to a connected elite, fed corruption, and pushed many Chinese and Indian Malaysians to emigrate. The NEP formally ended in 1990, but many of its preferences continue under later plans.
sum: An affirmative action programme in Malaysia, begun in 1971, that favoured ethnic Malays and other indigenous groups in business, education and jobs. It shaped the country for decades.
